vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-4372
vulnerability.description: HuggingFace transformers vulnerable to remote code execution

statements.impact_statement: transformers 4.57.6 is a BUILD-TIME-ONLY dependency of the isolated tools/model-export toolchain (hash-pinned export_env sidecar venv; SPEC §11 heavy-ML-closure isolation principle) and is NEVER installed in any shipped platform runtime image, container, or SBOM. CVE-2026-4372 is a remote-code-execution issue triggered by loading a model whose repository ships custom/remote code (trust_remote_code). tools/model-export/export_env/export_and_gate.py calls optimum.exporters.onnx.main_export() and sentence_transformers.SentenceTransformer() against a LOCAL, pre-downloaded, PINNED, trusted checkpoint (Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B @ 97b0c614be4d77ee51c0cef4e5f07c00f9eb65b3, a standard architecture registered natively by optimum-onnx) and NEVER passes trust_remote_code=True (it is left at its default of False). No untrusted or user-supplied model is ever loaded, so the vulnerable remote-code path is not reachable in our usage.

vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-1839

vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-9856
vulnerability.description: Transformers save_pretrained path traversal allows arbitrary file writes through chat template names

statements.impact_statement: transformers 4.57.6 is a build-time-only dependency of the isolated tools/model-export toolchain (hash-pinned export_env sidecar venv; SPEC §11 heavy-ML-closure isolation principle). The vulnerable save_pretrained() chat-template write path IS executed during an export, but every value that reaches it comes from a single SHA-pinned trusted checkpoint, so no adversary can control the chat-template names the CVE requires. EVIDENCE (re-verifiable without redoing the analysis; all versions are the hash-pinned tools/model-export/export_env/requirements.txt closure — optimum-onnx 0.1.0, optimum 2.1.0, transformers 4.57.6): (1) REACHABILITY IS CONCEDED — this statement deliberately does NOT claim vulnerable_code_not_in_execute_path. The sidecar's optimum.exporters.onnx.main_export() call (tools/model-export/export_env/export_and_gate.py) reaches transformers save_pretrained() transitively: optimum-onnx 0.1.0 src/optimum/exporters/onnx/convert.py line 1029 model.config.save_pretrained(output), line 1035 generation_config.save_pretrained(output), and line 1040 maybe_save_preprocessors(model_name_or_path, output) -> optimum 2.1.0 src/optimum/utils/save_utils.py line 92, which calls preprocessor.save_pretrained(dest_dir) for every loadable preprocessor INCLUDING the tokenizer — the exact function CVE-2026-9856 lives in (tokenizer save writes chat-template files whose names come from the tokenizer's chat-template config). (2) NO ADVERSARY CONTROL — the only model this tool can ever export is the single entry in the MODEL_SPECS registry (tools/model-export/src/ne/model_export/specs.py): Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B pinned at immutable commit 97b0c614be4d77ee51c0cef4e5f07c00f9eb65b3. export_and_gate.py resolves that revision to an immutable SHA via HfApi.repo_info (failing closed if it cannot) and snapshot_download()s exactly that revision; the CLI takes a registry key, never a user-supplied path or repo id. The chat-template names that flow into save_pretrained() therefore derive solely from that pinned, trusted snapshot — there is no input an adversary can control. (3) BUILD-TIME-ONLY — the deploy/docker/ne-app/Dockerfile runtime stage copies only /app/.venv, /bin/uv, the packages/ne-brain/parser_env payload, and the console dist: no tools/model-export content and no .export-venv ships in any runtime image, and transformers 4.57.6 appears in no platform uv.lock/SBOM. UPGRADE CONSTRAINT: the fixed release (5.10.0) is unreachable today — optimum-onnx 0.1.0 (the latest published release) requires transformers>=4.36,<4.58.0, so the bump is unsatisfiable until upstream ships optimum-onnx with transformers 5.x support; re-triage then.

vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-45829
vulnerability.description: chromadb: ChromaDB Python Project: Arbitrary code execution via pre-authentication code injection

statements.impact_statement: chromadb 1.1.1 is a BASE (unconditional, non-optional) dependency of the top-level `crewai` package (verified via crewai 1.15.5's PyPI requires_dist: `chromadb~=1.1.0` carries no `extra ==` marker), so it is pulled into packages/ne-mcp/crewai_env/ (the NE-CREWAI-DROPIN isolated sidecar venv, the out-of-process governed drop-in) regardless of whether CrewAI's optional memory feature is ever used. This CVE requires ChromaDB's Python/FastAPI HTTP server to be running and network-reachable pre-auth (confirmed via the public advisory: 'local installs... are not impacted'; 'affects internet-facing deployments'; the Rust frontend and local installs are explicitly out of scope). The sidecar's own code (packages/ne-mcp/crewai_env/agent.py) never references CrewAI's memory, embedder, or chromadb APIs at all (zero occurrences), never enables Agent(memory=True), and never starts any chromadb server process — chromadb is present in the venv purely as an unused transitive install, never imported or instantiated by anything this drop-in runs. No fixed version exists upstream as of 2026-07-22; re-verify this statement when chromadb ships a patch or when crewai's own pin range changes.

vulnerability.name: GHSA-xf7x-x43h-rpqh
vulnerability.description: json_repair: Circular JSON Schema $ref causes unbounded CPU DoS

statements.impact_statement: json-repair 0.25.3 is a BASE dependency of the top-level `crewai` package (crewai 1.15.5 pins `json-repair~=0.25.2` directly, tightly, with no `extra ==` marker — verified via PyPI requires_dist; the pin cannot be bumped past 0.25.x without diverging from crewai's own declared compatibility range). The vulnerable code is specifically `SchemaRepairer.resolve_schema()`, an unbounded loop resolving JSON Schema `$ref` references. CrewAI's own actual integration point (src/crewai/tools/tool_usage.py, verified via crewai's public source/PR history) calls only the unrelated `repair_json()` text-repair function to fix malformed LLM tool-call JSON output — never the schema-resolution code path. NE-CREWAI-DROPIN's own code (packages/ne-mcp/crewai_env/agent.py) never imports or calls json-repair directly either. The vulnerable function is present in the installed package but not reachable from any code path this drop-in or CrewAI's own tool-calling integration exercises. A fixed version (0.60.1+) exists upstream but cannot be adopted here because crewai's own pin caps it at <0.26.0; re-verify when crewai relaxes that pin.

vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-85734
vulnerability.description: lightrag-hku: No Rate Limiting on /login Endpoint Allows Brute-Force Attacks

statements.impact_statement: lightrag-hku 1.5.4 (wheel sha256 3bb28b2a763a91fb11b9ac87798140be852891edf71266cff59018d23afeea9d, the first hash at packages/ne-brain-graph/lightrag_env/requirements.txt:587) is installed ONLY in the isolated, hash-pinned LightRAG graph-retrieval sidecar venv compiled from packages/ne-brain-graph/lightrag_env/requirements.in; the string lightrag_env occurs 0 times in uv.lock, deploy/ and .github/, so no platform runtime, container image or SBOM carries it (packages/ne-brain-graph/tests/test_no_gpl_sidecar_leak.py; .importlinter contract t2-sidecars-out-of-process). CVE-2026-85734 is the absence of rate limiting on the bundled API server's POST /login handler, defined at lightrag/api/lightrag_server.py:2184 in the 1.5.4 wheel. That server is BANNED here and cannot even import: lightrag_server.py imports fastapi at lines 5-8, 22, 23, 26 and 72 and uvicorn at line 19, the wheel METADATA lists fastapi and uvicorn only under extra == "api" (METADATA lines 67 and 77), requirements.in pins lightrag-hku==1.5.4 with no extra, and the compiled closure (59 pins) contains no fastapi, uvicorn or starlette pin -- asserted from the parsed lockfile by packages/ne-brain-graph/tests/test_lightrag_sidecar_surface.py. At load, lightrag/__init__.py imports only typing and ._version (lines 1 and 3) and resolves LightRAG/QueryParam lazily from .lightrag (lines 27-40); lightrag/lightrag.py imports nothing under lightrag/api, and lightrag/api/__init__.py itself imports only .._version (line 1), so even a stray import of the lightrag.api package would not load lightrag_server.py. The only first-party code that imports lightrag is packages/ne-brain-graph/lightrag_env/project.py (imports LightRAG, lightrag.utils.EmbeddingFunc, lightrag.kg.shared_storage.initialize_pipeline_status; calls initialize_storages, ainsert_custom_kg, finalize_storages) and query.py (imports LightRAG, QueryParam; calls initialize_storages, aquery with only_need_context=True, finalize_storages); neither imports lightrag.api, AST-asserted by the same test. The sidecar is driven as a subprocess over JSON files by packages/ne-brain-graph/src/ne/brain_graph/lightrag/_lightrag.py (subprocess.run at lines 141-151 and 164-178) and opens no network listener, so no /login endpoint exists to brute-force. Fixed upstream in 1.5.5; 1.5.4 -> 1.5.x is an UPGRADE proposal for the weekly lane (SPEC 6.1.1 arbiter ruling 2026-09-23, Q1), not a security bump. REMOVE THIS STATEMENT if any first-party code imports lightrag.api, if fastapi/uvicorn/starlette enter the sidecar closure, or if the sidecar gains a network listener.

vulnerability.name: GHSA-frch-4w6v-q5xx
vulnerability.description: lightrag-hku: No Rate Limiting on /login Endpoint Allows Brute-Force Attacks

statements.impact_statement: Alias of CVE-2026-85734 (grype keys this finding by its GHSA id; vex_dualkey_gate.py matches vulnerability.name exactly, never aliases). Same evidence: the vulnerable POST /login handler lives in the bundled API server (lightrag/api/lightrag_server.py:2184 in the 1.5.4 wheel), which imports fastapi (lines 5-8, 22, 23, 26, 72) and uvicorn (line 19) -- packages that exist only under the wheel's extra == "api" (METADATA lines 67, 77) and are absent from the hash-pinned sidecar closure packages/ne-brain-graph/lightrag_env/requirements.txt (requirements.in pins lightrag-hku==1.5.4 with no extra). project.py and query.py import nothing from lightrag.api (AST-asserted by packages/ne-brain-graph/tests/test_lightrag_sidecar_surface.py), the sidecar runs as a subprocess over JSON files with no listener (packages/ne-brain-graph/src/ne/brain_graph/lightrag/_lightrag.py lines 141-151, 164-178), and lightrag_env is absent from uv.lock, deploy/ and .github/. Fixed upstream in 1.5.5; the bump is an UPGRADE proposal (arbiter 2026-09-23 Q1). Removal conditions as for CVE-2026-85734.

vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-85740
vulnerability.description: lightrag-hku: SSRF via IPv6-transition address bypass (NAT64, IPv4-compatible, 6to4) of the native-markdown image-download guard

statements.impact_statement: lightrag-hku 1.5.4 (wheel sha256 3bb28b2a763a91fb11b9ac87798140be852891edf71266cff59018d23afeea9d = packages/ne-brain-graph/lightrag_env/requirements.txt:587) is installed ONLY in the isolated, hash-pinned LightRAG sidecar venv; lightrag_env occurs 0 times in uv.lock, deploy/ and .github/. CVE-2026-85740 is an IPv6-transition-address (NAT64 64:ff9b::/96, IPv4-compatible ::/96, 6to4 2002::/16) bypass of _validated_addresses() at lightrag/parser/markdown/parser.py:241 (the ip.is_global check at line 268), which runs only inside that module: from _host_is_public (def line 274, calling it at 276), which NativeMarkdownParser._download (def line 503) calls at line 507 and the redirect handler calls at line 334, and from the pinned-connection resolver (line 286), all while ingesting an uploaded markdown/textpack DOCUMENT. In the 1.5.4 wheel that module is imported only lazily, inside NativeParser._markdown_parser at lightrag/parser/native_dispatch.py:47, which runs only from NativeParser.parse (native_dispatch.py:53-56); native_dispatch itself is loaded only by get_parser's importlib.import_module (lightrag/parser/registry.py:262; impl string lightrag.parser.native_dispatch:NativeParser at line 182). The document pipeline reaches it only through LightRAG.ainsert (lightrag/lightrag.py:1428; parser.routing import at 1479, apipeline_enqueue_documents at 1486, apipeline_process_enqueue_documents at 1493) -> lightrag/pipeline.py apipeline_process_enqueue_documents (line 927) -> _run_pipeline_batch (1075, def 1143) -> _parse_worker (1236, def 1546) -> get_parser (1647) -> parser.parse (1693). The sidecar never calls ainsert, insert, apipeline_enqueue_documents or apipeline_process_enqueue_documents and never parses a document: project.py calls only ainsert_custom_kg (lightrag/lightrag.py:1786-2052, whose body contains no import statement and no reference to lightrag.parser) on a JSON custom-KG payload, and query.py calls only aquery(..., only_need_context=True); both are AST-asserted by packages/ne-brain-graph/tests/test_lightrag_sidecar_surface.py. Stated honestly: lightrag.parser.base, lightrag.parser.registry and lightrag.parser.routing ARE imported at library load (lightrag.py:139 -> pipeline.py:44-54; lightrag.py:116 -> utils_pipeline.py:30), but lightrag/parser/registry.py loads no parser implementation until a document is parsed (registry.py:5-9), so lightrag/parser/markdown/parser.py is never imported, let alone executed, in the sidecar. No network-reachable input exists: the sidecar is a subprocess over JSON files (packages/ne-brain-graph/src/ne/brain_graph/lightrag/_lightrag.py lines 141-151, 164-178). Fixed upstream in 1.5.5; the bump is an UPGRADE proposal (SPEC 6.1.1 arbiter 2026-09-23 Q1). REMOVE THIS STATEMENT if first-party code calls ainsert/insert/apipeline_enqueue_documents or imports lightrag.parser, or if the sidecar gains a network listener.

vulnerability.name: GHSA-vv3m-f8x4-7377
vulnerability.description: lightrag-hku: SSRF via IPv6-transition address bypass (NAT64, IPv4-compatible, 6to4) of the native-markdown image-download guard

statements.impact_statement: Alias of CVE-2026-85740 (grype keys this finding by its GHSA id; vex_dualkey_gate.py matches vulnerability.name exactly, never aliases). Same evidence: the bypassed guard _validated_addresses() (lightrag/parser/markdown/parser.py:241, is_global check at 268) runs only inside that module (NativeMarkdownParser._download def 503 -> _host_is_public check at 507), a module imported lazily by lightrag/parser/native_dispatch.py:47 from the document-ingestion pipeline (LightRAG.ainsert lightrag.py:1428 -> pipeline.py apipeline_process_enqueue_documents 927 -> _parse_worker 1546 -> parser.parse 1693). The sidecar's project.py calls only ainsert_custom_kg (lightrag.py:1786-2052; no parser import in its body) and query.py only aquery(only_need_context=True); neither calls ainsert/insert/apipeline_enqueue_documents nor imports lightrag.parser (AST-asserted by packages/ne-brain-graph/tests/test_lightrag_sidecar_surface.py); the sidecar is a subprocess over JSON files with no listener (_lightrag.py lines 141-151, 164-178); lightrag_env is absent from uv.lock, deploy/ and .github/. Fixed upstream in 1.5.5; bump is an UPGRADE proposal (arbiter 2026-09-23 Q1). Removal conditions as for CVE-2026-85740.
